messages:
incident-bot: Paging on-call: streaming responses SLO breach detected in prod-usw2, latency p99 > 2.5s for last 10m. @sara you're oncall — please ack.

sara: ack. seeing increased token queue depth and >85% GPU mem on a few dedicated pools.

miguel: on it. any specific customer-facing errors?

sara: not many 5xxs, mostly timeouts and client-observed stalls on SSE. metrics: in-flight streams spiking when burst > 1200rps.

tess: suspect prefix caching thrash + continuous-batching causing head-of-line latencies. might be cheaper to force synchronous (non-stream) path for a bit.

danny: agree. can we flip streaming=false at gateway level so requests fall back to single-response generation? that should dramatically lower handshake/keepalive overhead.

ops-robot: Suggested mitigations: 1) throttle streaming route to 10rps per customer, 2) rollback public free-tier burst quotas to baseline, 3) toggle streaming off for production global for 15m with graceful fallback.

sara: priority: stabilize p99 latency immediately. I want the least customer-visible disruption. fallback to non-stream is acceptable. start with a canary (10% traffic) then 100% if stable.

miguel: prepping toggle. command to run on control plane (runbook):

```
# disable streaming route
curl -X POST https://control.redwood.internal/api/feature-toggle -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" -d '{"feature":"streaming_responses","state":"partial_disable","percent":10}'

# after validation, set percent to 100
```

tess: add a temporary rate-limit rule too: `x-route: streaming` -> 10rps/customer. That protects customers from noisy neighbors while we evaluate.

support-bot: Creating status page draft: "We are temporarily falling back to non-streaming responses to improve latency for all customers. Some streaming clients may see a change in behavior; responses are still delivered but not as incremental chunks." Will hold publish until ops confirms.

sara: miguel, run the 10% toggle. I'll watch dashboards and traces. notify cust-facing teams.

miguel: executing now.

ops-robot: feature-toggle audit: user=miguel, action=partial_disable, feature=streaming_responses, percent=10, ts=1868123501

miguel: canaries look good for 5m. p95 down ~450ms, p99 trending down. No client errors in canary group.

sara: ramping to 100% disable. miguel, proceed.

miguel: executing percent=100.

ops-robot: feature-toggle audit: user=miguel, action=partial_disable, feature=streaming_responses, percent=100, ts=1868123589

sara: all streaming routes now forced to non-stream path. immediate p99 drop to 1.1s. GPU mem usage normalized.

danny: rolling back free-tier burst quotas by 30% to reduce surge risk while we monitor. command: `quota-manager set --tier free --burst 0.7`

ops-robot: quota update applied (user=danny, tier=free, old=1.0, new=0.7, ts=1868123610)

tess: quick check: any major customers reporting broken clients? some clients expect chunked data; they may see behavior change. need to surface in support.

support-bot: Notified support channels and created an internal ticket for impacted SDK customers. suggested mitigation: SDK v2 will auto-handle single-response payloads but older SDKs may need a small patch.

miguel: aggregating logs: about 0.4% of active sessions show SSE disconnects during toggle; most reconnect and receive full payload via fallback.

sara: happy with mitigation. let's keep streaming disabled for 30 minutes and observe. if stable, we can plan a staged reenable with updated batching heuristics.

danny: I'll push a temporary config change to increase KV cache TTL for 10 minutes to reduce cache churn while disabled.

ops-robot: KV cache ttl updated user=danny ttl_sec=900 ts=1868123725

support-bot: Status page draft ready and will be published now: "Investigating degraded streaming performance; temporarily routing traffic to non-streaming responses to stabilize latency. Customers may notice a change in response delivery. Engineers are monitoring; follow updates here."

sara: publishing is fine. Also send a short note to enterprise customers with dedicated pools so SRE has point contacts if they see anomalies.

miguel: reaching out to top 10 enterprise customers now. so far only a couple asked clarifying q's, none are blocked.

tess: action items for postmortem: 1) root cause of streaming path CPU/mem spike, 2) revisit batching and prefix cache eviction policy, 3) add circuit-breaker for streaming route when queue depth threshold reached, 4) SDK compatibility doc for non-stream fallback.

sara: adding: telemetry hook to differentiate streaming vs non-stream latencies in traces, and a runbook decision tree for streaming toggles (canary -> metrics -> ramp).

danny: will draft the emergency toggle script with safety checks and an abort flow.

ops-robot: monitoring note: continue 1m polling for next 30m. alerts suppressed for streaming route SLO during mitigation window (user=sara).

support-bot: internal update sent to #customer-success with recommended message templates for customers using streaming.

miguel: 15m after full disable: p99 stable at ~1.05s, error budget healthy. no regression spikes observed.

sara: good. keep disabled for another 15m then start gradual reenable with 5% increments and the new rate-limit in place. tests must pass on canary.

ops-robot: Note for post-incident: record exact timeline and all toggles for audit.

support-bot: Ticket created: INC-2026-00134 with summary "Transient streaming path overload -> temporary non-stream fallback" assigned to miguel, tess, danny.

miguel: thanks. I'll start the postmortem draft and include logs, traces, and the control-plane toggles.

sara: good work. leaving the thread open for 1h. If anything regresses, re-ping with severity. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident state changed to mitigated (mitigation=streaming forced non-stream fallback + quota rollback). acknowledged_by=sara, mitigated_ts=1868123920
